answer: Spaced-arrival gating: each identity must emit actions across a minimum wall-clock spread, checked through a local prism of arrival timestamps rather than counts. The enforcement rule rejects identities whose inter-arrival delta falls below a threshold calibrated to genuine human pacing, so a batch spun up at once fails inspection. A sparrow of activity spread thinly over hours passes, while any clone farm must pay the per-identity cost of holding each account open and dripped for that full window, multiplying attacker wall-clock time and idle infrastructure by the number of sybils sought.
